case.title: Generator and analyzer crash on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
case.head: ju26-issue-2283
case.author: agent (commit 9df83c38, branch ju26-issue-2283)

issue_text:
# #2283 Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

In that case the consuming assembly still gets its generated resolver.

Diagnostics for types declared in the compiling project are unchanged.

units.name: Generic types from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

units.summary: Tells users that closed generics from other assemblies work, and that problems in such a type are reported only by its defining project.

checks.claim: No live code in TypeCollector.cs indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] any more (commented-out code excluded).
The issue's third site survives only as a commented-out line.
Both sites the change touches now use a null-safe lookup.
The generator calls TypeCollector with no reporter, so the new filter cannot change generated code.

Diagnostic call sites in TypeCollector that now pass through the filter (count).
The filter keeps a diagnostic only if it has a source location inside this compilation, so a diagnostic with no location is dropped too.
The neighbouring MemberNeedsKey path handles properties declared by a record parameter (ParameterSyntax).

checks.claim: All three new tests go through the shared metadata-reference helper.
The helper asserts that the resolver was generated, not only that nothing crashed.
The defining source is emitted to an image and referenced as metadata, the boundary the bug needs.
Compilations honour the requested language version (record structs need C# 10+).
The added usings are used: the tests resolve .NET 8 reference assemblies.
The new tests declare only properties, no fields.
The second changed site sits in the loop over fields.
In-source MsgPack004 analyzer tests exist that would catch a dropped in-source diagnostic, if run.
The unkeyed test's referenced type has a public property with no Key attribute.
MsgPack004 is an Error, so the filter can silence errors, not just warnings.

refusals.question: Should TypeCollector drop every diagnostic located outside this compilation, or only those about symbols that come from metadata?
refusals.why: It looks like a one-line plumbing change, but it changes what users are warned about across every analyzer rule, errors included, not only the crash path in the issue. The unkeyed-member test passes because of this filter, not because of the crash fix: before the change that path already reported MsgPack004 instead of crashing. Whether a lost error is acceptable is a decision about the analyzer's contract, and the existing analyzer suite that would show the cost has not been run.
options: Narrow the filter to symbols with no syntax and keep diagnostics without a location

refusals.question: Do we promise users that problems in a referenced type are reported only by the project that defines it?
refusals.why: The issue asks for no crash and a generated resolver. It says nothing about where diagnostics for referenced types belong. The agent wrote a behaviour guarantee into the README and the MsgPack004 docs and locked it in a test. The promise holds only if the defining project runs the analyzer. If it is a third-party package, nobody in the consuming project is told. Publishing a guarantee is the maintainers' call.
refusals.agent_choice: Document and test the silence as intended behaviour.
